A.summary:
This commit replaces the prototype Linux bug pipeline with a staged,
asynchronous workflow. Submitting a candidate bug now only stores it as a
raw database row, and a new background BugWorker later runs it through the
pipeline. The goal is to exit early on false positives and duplicates, keep
the slow LLM stages concurrent, and keep full traceability of each bug.

The worker runs these stages in order. Verification checks the bug against
mainline top-of-trunk. Normalization sets a canonical title and subsystem
using git tools and MAINTAINERS hints. Deduplication runs under a global
lock. For novel bugs only, enrichment then traces the origin commit,
estimates severity, and writes a plain-text LKML-style report.

The commit also adds the raw_input and verified_on_sha columns to the bugs
table, so the original request payload is kept as a JSON blob. It extends
update_bug_outcome to carry the normalized fields, and adds a design
document and unit tests.

User-visible effect: bugs found during patch review are no longer fully
processed inline. They are queued with status "raw" and finalized later by
the worker. Stored bug records now carry a normalized title, a single
canonical subsystem, a calibrated severity, a standalone report, and an
origin commit. False positives and processing errors are recorded as
"dismissed" or "failed".

Before:
  A candidate bug was processed during the call and was stored as a
  finished record with its original problem text.

After:
  A candidate bug is stored at once with status "raw" and its original
  request JSON. The bug worker later updates it to "open" (with canonical
  title, subsystem, severity, report, and origin commit), "dismissed"
  (false positive), or "failed" (processing error), or marks it as a
  duplicate of an existing bug.
A.inline_review:
- [HIGH] Commit message adds the Linux bug-discovery stage prompts in
  src/workflows/linux_bug.rs (VerifySession::system_prompt and the
  normalization and severity prompts) with no benchmark or local re-review
  evidence. The anti-charity validation filter decides which candidates
  are dismissed as false positives, and the other prompts shape every
  stored bug, so detection rate and precision may regress unnoticed.

- [MEDIUM] In src/worker/bug_worker.rs (BugWorker::run) and
  src/workflows/linux_bug.rs (process_issue), BugInput.reasoning is rebuilt
  from bug.severity_explanation, which process_issue always inserts as
  None. Every queued bug runs verification, normalization and tracing with
  the placeholder 'No reasoning provided.'. The reporter's reasoning
  survives only in raw_input, which is written but never deserialized.
  Tests pass the original input and miss this.

- [MEDIUM] In src/workflows/linux_bug.rs (process_issue_worker),
  BUG_DEDUP_LOCK is released at the end of the Stage 3 block, but
  vector_json and status open are written only in Stage 7, after the
  unlocked tracing, severity and report stages.
  list_all_bugs_for_vector_search returns only open, fixed and verified
  rows, so two concurrent identical candidates can both pass deduplication
  and be registered as separate bugs.

- [MEDIUM] In src/worker/bug_worker.rs (BugWorker::run), a detached
  tokio::spawn is created per claimed raw bug with no semaphore or
  JoinSet, and the loop sleeps only when the queue is empty. A backlog
  starts one multi-stage pipeline (up to 50 turns per stage) per bug at
  once, risking provider rate-limit storms, runaway token spend and git
  and database contention.

- [MEDIUM] The new pipeline is not wired up. BugWorker is never
  constructed or spawned (no use in src/main.rs or src/reviewer.rs), and
  process_issue in src/workflows/linux_bug.rs has no non-test caller.
  link_review_to_bug is never called by the new flow, so the deferred
  review linking promised by the design is not implemented. process_issue
  also returns NewlyDiscovered for a bug that is only queued with status
  raw, which would mislabel dismissed or duplicate bugs for a future
  caller.

- [MEDIUM] In src/db.rs (Database::mark_bug_as_duplicate), the INSERT OR
  IGNORE INTO review_bugs omits is_newly_discovered, so the schema default
  of 1 applies and reviews migrated to the canonical bug are marked as
  newly discovered. The design requires 0 for duplicates, and
  migrate_review_bugs already inserts 0 in the same situation.

- [MEDIUM] In src/db.rs (Database::lock_raw_bug), the claim is a SELECT of
  a raw row followed by an UPDATE to processing with no status = raw guard
  and no rows-affected check, so two workers sharing a database can claim
  the same row. Nothing resets stale processing rows after a restart, a
  task panic or cancellation. In src/worker/bug_worker.rs
  (BugWorker::run), the failed-status write is 'let _ =' and unlogged, so
  a failed write also leaves the row in processing. Such bugs silently
  never reach a terminal state.

- [MEDIUM] In src/db.rs (Database::mark_bug_as_duplicate), the transaction
  is opened with self.conn.transaction() on the connection shared by all
  tasks, with no tx_lock or guard. Concurrent BugWorker tasks, and
  update_bug_outcome calls made outside BUG_DEDUP_LOCK, can hit a
  nested-transaction error, which marks the bug failed and loses the
  duplicate link, or can have their autocommit statements absorbed into
  and rolled back with this transaction.

- [MEDIUM] In src/db.rs (Database::lock_raw_bug), the poll 'WHERE status =
  raw ORDER BY created_at LIMIT 1' has no supporting index on
  bugs(status, created_at), so each poll scans and sorts the table.
  Database::list_all_bugs_for_vector_search has no LIMIT and no status
  index, and parse_bug_row decompresses inline_review and logs for every
  row. This runs inside BUG_DEDUP_LOCK, so cost grows with the total bug

- [LOW] In src/db.rs (Database::update_bug_outcome), only problem,
  subsystems, source_files and locations use COALESCE. Severity,
  severity_explanation, inline_review, logs, vector_json,
  introduced_in_commit, verified_on_sha, is_fixed and fixed_in_commit are

findings.explanation: Verification, normalization and tracing silently run with the placeholder 'No reasoning provided.' instead of the reporter's reasoning, which degrades verification quality with no error. process_issue inserts the row with severity_explanation None and keeps the reasoning only inside the raw_input JSON. BugWorker::run rebuilds BugInput.reasoning from bug.severity_explanation, so every queued bug gets the placeholder. baseline_sha is only a copy of discovered_in_commit. raw_input is written and selected but never deserialized, so the immutable-ingestion goal is unused. findings.problem: BUG_DEDUP_LOCK released before novel bug is dedup-visible
findings.explanation: Two concurrent identical candidates can both pass deduplication and both be registered as separate open bugs, leaving duplicate canonical rows. The guard lives only in the Stage 3 block. vector_json and status open are written only in Stage 7, after the unlocked tracing, severity and report LLM stages. list_all_bugs_for_vector_search returns only open, fixed and verified rows and the current row is filtered out, so an in-flight bug is invisible to a concurrent Stage 3. The lock serializes comparisons but not the check-then-register gap, contradicting design section 1.1 item 4. Likelihood depends on concurrent finds of the same defect, hence Medium.

findings.explanation: BugWorker::run claims a raw bug, calls tokio::spawn and loops again immediately with no semaphore or JoinSet; it sleeps only when the queue is empty. A backlog of raw bugs starts one multi-stage pipeline per bug at once, each with up to 50 turns per stage plus git tool calls on the shared repository. Consequences are provider rate-limit storms, runaway token spend and database and git contention, contrary to resource-limits.md. Capped at Medium because nothing in this diff starts the worker yet.

findings.problem: linux_bug verification prompts added without validation evidence
findings.explanation: Reasoning: the commit introduces the Linux bug-discovery stage instructions in src/workflows/linux_bug.rs. These decide which candidate bugs are dismissed as false positives, how they are titled and classified, and how severity is assigned. That affects the detection rate and precision of Linux bug discovery across the board, so review-core priority 5 and severity.md (High) require benchmark or re-review results in the commit message. The full commit message is a bullet list of features (Verification with anti-charity validation, Normalization, Deduplication, enrichment, raw_input persistence, bug worker). It contains no benchmark results, no local re-review results, and no comparison of false-positive or detection rates. The Deduplication exemption (DedupSession, BUG_DEDUP_LOCK) covers only Stage 3 and does not extend to the other stages. VerifySession::system_prompt (the CRITICAL VALIDATION FILTER telling the model not to give the code the benefit of the doubt) and the Stage 1 early exit that marks candidates 'dismissed' are Linux bug-discovery stage instructions and are not exempt. The Normalization and Severity prompts shape the stored title, subsystem and severity of every bug. This is not post-triage maintenance on already-triaged bugs: the pipeline is the triage of newly discovered candidates. Not a benchmarks/ file demand: the finding is only that the commit message lacks validation evidence, and it does not ask for any change to benchmarks/. The defect is in the commit message, so it is not preexisting.

findings.explanation: Reasoning: the new pipeline is dead code at the series end. Nothing breaks for existing reviews, and the cost is a feature that silently never runs plus a design/commit-message promise that is not met, so this is Medium. Greps at 313bdbe: BugWorker appears only in src/worker/bug_worker.rs and the 'pub mod bug_worker;' line in src/worker/mod.rs. There is no construction or spawn in src/main.rs (no matches for linux_bug|BugWorker|bug_worker|create_bug). src/reviewer.rs has no matches for linux_bug::|create_bug(|bug_worker, so it was not touched. process_issue (the only code that inserts a 'raw' bug) is called only from #[cfg(test)] tests in linux_bug.rs. db.link_review_to_bug is called only from a db.rs test (about line 10258), never by the new flow. findings.problem: mark_bug_as_duplicate links migrated reviews as newly discovered
findings.explanation: Reasoning: this is a concrete state bug in the new duplicate path. It affects review/bug linkage metadata for individual bugs, with no crash or data loss, so Medium. mark_bug_as_duplicate, called from process_issue_worker on a duplicate verdict, runs 'INSERT OR IGNORE INTO review_bugs (review_id, bug_id) SELECT review_id, ?1 FROM review_bugs WHERE bug_id = ?2' without setting is_newly_discovered. The schema default is 'is_newly_discovered INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1', so the review gets linked to the canonical bug as newly discovered, which contradicts the design (duplicates linked with is_newly_discovered = 0). The existing migrate_review_bugs helper in the same file explicitly inserts 0, so the correct behaviour was available. Because INSERT OR IGNORE keeps any existing row, a review already linked to the canonical bug keeps its old value. Readers (get_reviews_bugs paths using row.get(21).unwrap_or(1)) will report the duplicate as newly discovered once any review is linked to the ephemeral bug.

locations.why_this_location_matters: It omits is_newly_discovered, so the schema default of 1 applies to the migrated link. migrate_review_bugs sets 0 in the same situation.

findings.problem: raw bug claim is non-atomic and stale processing rows are never recovered
findings.explanation: Reasoning: the effect is confined to individual bug rows, which get stuck. The failure needs a daemon restart, a task panic, or a failed status write while a bug is being processed. No other data is corrupted, so this is a contained state-lifecycle bug (Medium). (1) Database::lock_raw_bug (src/db.rs:1362) runs 'SELECT id FROM bugs WHERE status = raw ... LIMIT 1' and then 'UPDATE bugs SET status = processing WHERE id = ?'. The UPDATE has no 'AND status = raw' guard, and its rows-affected count is never checked. This is the SELECT-then-unconditional-UPDATE TOCTOU pattern that patterns/concurrency.md section 1 item 4 forbids. Within a single BugWorker loop the claim is effectively serialized, because the loop awaits lock_raw_bug before spawning and the claimed row is no longer raw on the next iteration. Two BugWorkers or daemons sharing one database could claim the same row, though. The concurrency guide says the in-process model is the only supported one, so I treat double-claim as a latent risk and not the main defect. (2) Stale rows: git_grep over src/ for processing and locked_by finds only the claim UPDATE at src/db.rs:1374. No startup sweep, lease, timeout, or locked_by column exists to reset processing rows, even though the concurrency guide says locked_by is recorded for crash recovery. A bug claimed by a task that is interrupted stays in processing forever, since lock_raw_bug selects only raw rows. The interrupting events are a daemon restart or shutdown (tokio::spawn tasks are cancelled), or a panic inside the spawned task; the JoinHandle is dropped in BugWorker::run, so a panic is unobserved. (3) The Err arm in BugWorker::run writes the failed status with 'let _ = db.update_bug_outcome(...)'. If that write fails (for example SQLITE_BUSY), the row also stays in processing with no log, which is the swallowed-error pattern in patterns/error-handling.md section 2. (4) Supervision: git_grep for BugWorker and spawn_supervised_worker across src/ finds BugWorker only in src/worker/bug_worker.rs, with no spawn_supervised_worker call and no construction site. At this commit nothing visibly wires or supervises the worker, so a panic in run() would not be restarted. I could not confirm whether wiring arrives later, because only this single commit was available. The get_bug question: get_bug returns Ok(None) only if the row is missing, and rows are never deleted here, so the expect in process_issue_worker is not a real hazard. Net effect: affected bugs silently never reach open, dismissed, or duplicate, and they look identical to bugs still in progress. Not Low, because the loss is silent.

locations.why_this_location_matters: Claim is not conditioned on status = 'raw', rows affected are not checked, and no code anywhere resets processing rows.
The only terminal-state write on error is best-effort and unlogged; the spawned JoinHandle is dropped, so panics and cancellation also leave the row in processing.

findings.problem: mark_bug_as_duplicate opens a transaction on the shared connection
findings.explanation: Reasoning: the failure is a localized concurrency defect. It affects individual bugs being deduplicated, needs overlapping DB activity on the shared libsql handle, and is not a daemon-wide outage or data-destroying bug, so Medium. Verification: at revision 313bdbe6 git_grep finds no tx_lock and no DatabaseTransaction in src/db.rs. begin_transaction exists at src/db.rs:2083, but it is a bare async fn that runs BEGIN IMMEDIATE on self.conn with no lock and no guard. mark_bug_as_duplicate (src/db.rs:1535) calls self.conn.transaction().await? directly at line 1547, so the transaction runs on the connection every other task shares. Its only caller is process_issue_worker (src/workflows/linux_bug.rs:972), which this commit adds. BugWorker::run in the new src/worker/bug_worker.rs spawns one tokio task per raw bug with no concurrency cap, and those tasks share Arc<Database> with the ingestor, email and patchwork workers and the HTTP handlers. BUG_DEDUP_LOCK serializes only the dedup stage among BugWorker tasks. It does not exclude other components, and it does not exclude update_bug_outcome, which the same tasks call outside the lock. On a single sqlite3 handle, a second BEGIN while another task's transaction is open fails with a nested-transaction error. That error propagates through ? and BugWorker marks the bug failed, so the duplicate link is lost and the bug is left in status failed. Autocommit statements from other tasks can also be absorbed into this transaction and be rolled back with it. Caveat: the guideline's DatabaseTransaction / tx_lock mechanism does not exist at this revision, so the fix cannot simply be to switch to begin_transaction. The shared-handle hazard is the same, and the transaction needs to be serialized by a lock or a dedicated connection. Preexisting is false because the commit introduces the concurrent BugWorker call path that relies on this function; the function body itself is unchanged.

locations.why_this_location_matters: Opens a transaction directly on the connection shared by all concurrent tasks, with no tx_lock or DatabaseTransaction guard.
Only caller, newly reachable from concurrently spawned BugWorker tasks, which also run update_bug_outcome outside BUG_DEDUP_LOCK.

locations.why_this_location_matters: The only begin_transaction at this revision is an unguarded BEGIN IMMEDIATE on the same shared handle, so it would collide with mark_bug_as_duplicate.

findings.problem: unindexed raw-bug poll and unbounded bug load under dedup lock
findings.explanation: Reasoning: this is a scalability defect on a continuously growing table. It causes no immediate failure, data loss, or wrong output, and it degrades throughput as the bugs table grows, so Medium fits. (1) Database::lock_raw_bug (src/db.rs:1362-1382) runs 'SELECT id FROM bugs WHERE status = 'raw' ORDER BY created_at ASC LIMIT 1'. The only bugs indexes at this commit are idx_bugs_slug, idx_bugs_severity and idx_bugs_is_fixed (src/db.rs:889-895, src/schema.sql:311-313). Nothing covers status or created_at, so every poll is a full scan of bugs plus a sort. BugWorker::run polls every 5 seconds when idle and immediately again after each claimed bug. The cost grows with every bug ever stored, even though almost all rows are no longer 'raw'. The db-migrations guide requires an explicit index on any column used in WHERE or ORDER BY on the bugs table, and this commit introduces the status='raw' queue pattern without one. (2) Database::list_all_bugs_for_vector_search (src/db.rs:1709-1730) selects every row with status IN ('open','fixed','verified') and has no LIMIT. It also has no status index, so it scans the whole table. For every returned row, parse_bug_row (src/db.rs:1732+) calls get_compressed_string_opt on column 9 (inline_review) and column 10 (logs). Both are stored through compress_string_if_needed and can be large, since logs is the serialized full multi-stage turn history, so each is decompressed and materialized as a String. The query also loads raw_input and locations even though only the sparse vector and a few fields are needed for candidate retrieval. process_issue_worker calls this inside the BUG_DEDUP_LOCK critical section (Stage 3), once per bug, and holds the lock through the LLM dedup call. The load is therefore O(total bugs x size of logs and reviews) in time and memory, per processed bug, and it serializes all concurrent bug workers behind it. This violates the resource-limits invariant that queries on growing tables must be bounded or paginated. The patch adds both the new polling query and the new per-bug call pattern: the extra SELECT columns, the new 'raw'/'processing' states, and the per-bug invocation under the global lock. Hence preexisting is false. Fix: add an index on bugs(status, created_at), and make the vector-search loader select only the id, slug, severity, subsystems, source_files, problem, and vector_json columns it needs without decompressing inline_review and logs.

findings.problem: tracing SHA validated as any commit-ish, not a full SHA
findings.type: Git Argument Injection / Unvalidated Model Output
findings.explanation: Reasoning: the option-injection part of the concern does not hold, but a narrower real defect remains with limited blast radius. TracingSession::validate runs git cat-file -e with a single argv element, format!("{}^{{commit}}", sha). A model-supplied value starting with '-' becomes an unknown option such as '-x^{commit}', so git exits non-zero and validation rejects it. Since Command::new('git').args([...]) uses no shell, no flag injection reaches format_commit. The remaining problem is that the check only proves the string resolves to a commit-ish. Branch names, tags, HEAD, HEAD~N and abbreviated SHAs all pass. The stage prompt and the design document both require an exact 40-character SHA, and nothing enforces it. The model output is steerable by the reported patch text. format_commit then stores the raw string, not the resolved SHA, in introduced_in_commit, so the bug record can hold a moving ref such as 'master' or a short hash. That ref changes meaning over time and is shown as 'Introduced in commit' in the LKML report. The check also runs only if tools is Some. bug_worker always passes Some, so in production the gap is limited to the weak check. Impact is incorrect or unstable origin attribution on individual bug records, not a security boundary breach. Fix: require a 40-hex (or 64-hex) string before cat-file, add '--end-of-options' or use 'git rev-parse --verify', and store the resolved full SHA. Also, validate uses blocking std::process::Command inside an async session.

findings.problem: linux_bug sessions lack the duplicate tool-call guard
findings.explanation: Reasoning: the cost is wasted provider calls and tokens, bounded by max_turns, with no crash, data loss or wrong output, so Low. VerifySession, NormalizeSession and TracingSession in src/workflows/linux_bug.rs each implement call_tool as a bare tools.call(name, args) and do not override call_tools. They therefore inherit the LlmSession::call_tools default in src/ai/session.rs, which loops over the calls and invokes call_tool. That default has no duplicate check and no last_tool_call state. The only guard in the tree is StageSession::call_tool and StageSession::call_tools in src/workflow/stage.rs, backed by the last_tool_call field, which returns "Duplicate tool call blocked. Please change parameters or use a different tool." workflow-engine.md section 6 requires every new LlmSession that runs tools to carry this guard. The only bound left is max_turns: process_issue_worker uses with_max_turns(50) for verification, normalization and dedup, and 30 for tracing. A model that keeps re-issuing the same git_grep or git_read_files call gets a real result each time instead of the corrective error, and can use the whole budget. That is up to 50 provider calls per bug with ever-growing history, and the daemon-side BugWorker spawns a task per raw bug with no concurrency cap. Error handling is fine, since the default call_tools turns tool errors into {"error": ...}. The last turn is tool-free, so the loop terminates. The cost is wasted tokens and latency only. This is code the patch adds, so it is not preexisting.

B.summary:
This change replaces the prototype Linux kernel bug pipeline in Sashiko
with a staged, asynchronous one. Candidate bugs are first stored as raw
rows with the original request kept as JSON. A new background BugWorker
then runs them through verification, normalization, deduplication and
enrichment. This keeps the input traceable, drops false positives and
duplicates early, and spends git tracing and report generation only on
confirmed novel bugs.

Before:
  process_issue ran the whole analysis inline for a candidate bug.
  There was no raw_input column, and review_bugs links could be created
  before the bug was confirmed. update_bug_outcome took eleven
  positional arguments and never rewrote the title, subsystems, source
  files or locations.

After:
  process_issue only inserts a bug row with status "raw", storing the
  request as raw_input JSON, and returns NewlyDiscovered with that
  queued row. BugWorker polls lock_raw_bug every 5 seconds and spawns a
  task per bug that calls process_issue_worker. That function runs
  these stages:
    1. Verification against the mainline master SHA. A proven false
       positive sets status "dismissed" and the pipeline stops.
    2. Normalization to a canonical title, subsystem and source files,
       with a MAINTAINERS subsystem hint.
    3. Deduplication under a global BUG_DEDUP_LOCK mutex. It does a
       vector top-20 search at a 0.65 threshold, then an LLM check. A
       duplicate is recorded through mark_bug_as_duplicate and the
       pipeline stops.
    4. Origin tracing, which validates the introducing commit SHA with
       git cat-file.
    5. Severity estimation (Low, Medium, High, Critical or Unknown).
    6. A plain-text LKML-style report, generated without tools.
    7. A final write that sets status "open", the canonical fields, the
       vector, the report, the origin commit, verified_on_sha and logs.
  If processing errors out, the worker marks the bug "failed" and
  stores the error message in severity_explanation.

Supporting changes:
  - The bugs table gains status, verified_on_sha and raw_input columns,
    in both the schema and the migrations. The Bug and NewBug structs
    carry raw_input.
  - Every bug SELECT and row parser is updated for the new column
    order.
  - update_bug_outcome now takes an UpdateBugOutcomeParams struct. Its
    optional fields use COALESCE, so unset values keep existing data.
  - Severity gains a Default of Unknown.
  - A design document describing the pipeline is added.
  - Unit tests cover the verification, normalization, dedup, report and
    end-to-end flows using mock AI providers.

findings.problem: raw bugs stuck in processing forever after restart or failed write
findings.explanation: Consequence: a candidate bug claimed by BugWorker::run is silently lost, with no retry, no failed status and no log line, whenever the process stops or the task panics between the claim and the final status write. Reachability: this is every restart, deploy or crash while a bug is in flight, and each pipeline run is long (up to 50 LLM turns in Stage 1, plus Stages 2 to 6). Database::lock_raw_bug (src/db.rs:1362-1377) selects only status = 'raw' and moves the row to 'processing' with a separate UPDATE. A grep of src at 313bdbe for 'processing' finds no code that resets, leases or times out processing rows: the only matches are that UPDATE and an unrelated comment about duplicate patchset messages. BugWorker is also only defined in src/worker/bug_worker.rs, so nothing else touches the state. The recovery path in BugWorker::run writes the failed status with let _ = db.update_bug_outcome(...), so if that write errors (database unavailable, which is also the likeliest reason the pipeline failed) the row stays in processing. A panic inside the spawned tokio task also skips it entirely. Rows in processing are never selected again, so the bug is neither retried nor marked failed, and anyone reading the bugs table sees an in-progress item. This is a silent failure per patterns/silent-failure.md (error mapped to nothing, state indistinguishable from real progress). Double claim (the first half of the candidate) is not proven: the SELECT and the UPDATE are separate statements with no status guard and no rows-affected check, so a second claimer (another process on the same libsql URL, or a second BugWorker) could take the same row. I found no second claimer in this tree, so that part is unconfirmed and depends on how the service is deployed; the stuck-row part stands independently of it. Fix: claim with a single UPDATE ... WHERE id = (SELECT ... status = 'raw' ...) AND status = 'raw' RETURNING, and reset or lease-expire processing rows on startup.

findings.problem: BUG_DEDUP_LOCK held across LLM call with no overall timeout
findings.explanation: Consequence: one hung or slow dedup LLM call stalls Stage 3 for every queued bug, so no bug can reach 'open' or be marked duplicate until it returns. Reachability: process_issue_worker takes BUG_DEDUP_LOCK, then runs a DB scan (list_all_bugs_for_vector_search) and 'runner.run(&mut dedup_session).await?' while the guard is held. BugWorker::run spawns one task per raw bug with no concurrency bound, so every other task waits on that lock after Stage 2. The lock is intentional per the design doc, but the hold time is not bounded by the code. Verification: SessionRunner::run (src/ai/session.rs) has no timeout of its own. It only caps turns, validation attempts (3), and transient retries (5), each retry sleeping for retry_after. Per-request timeouts depend on the provider. Present: gemini (600s), ollama, openai and vllm (api_timeout_secs), and the claude/codex/copilot/devin CLI wrappers (600s) and kiro (timeout_secs). Absent: ClaudeClient (src/ai/claude.rs) and the Vertex client (src/ai/vertex.rs) both use 'client: Client::new()', which has no request timeout, so a stalled connection there holds the guard indefinitely. I found no timeout in bedrock.rs and did not confirm one. Even where timeouts exist, the worst case is roughly 600s per attempt across up to 3 validation and 5 transient attempts, with every other bug waiting. Mitigation: wrap the dedup run in tokio::time::timeout inside the critical section, and give the Claude/Vertex clients a request timeout. Capped at Medium because the unbounded case depends on which provider is configured, and I did not check the BackoffProvider wiring for those providers.

findings.problem: mark_bug_as_duplicate transaction shares one libsql connection
findings.explanation: Consequence: while mark_bug_as_duplicate has a transaction open, writes from other tasks on the same connection become part of it. They commit with it, or are silently rolled back if any statement in it fails and the transaction is dropped. A concurrent transaction() call fails on a nested BEGIN. Reachability: Database holds one libsql::Connection (pub conn: libsql::Connection). Database::new builds it once with db.connect() and returns Self { conn }, with no pool and no mutex. Every user shares it through Arc<Database>: api.rs, ingestor.rs, reviewer.rs, worker/patchwork.rs, worker/compressor.rs and main.rs. mark_bug_as_duplicate calls self.conn.transaction() on this connection and then runs tx.execute for the UPDATE, INSERT OR IGNORE and DELETE, so nothing excludes other statements on it. This commit adds BugWorker::run, which tokio::spawns an unbounded task per raw bug. Each task calls update_bug_outcome (stage 1 dismissal, stage 7 'open' write, the failure handler), get_bug and others on the same connection. BUG_DEDUP_LOCK is held only inside process_issue_worker stage 3, so it serializes dedup writers against each other but not against these other statements, the lock_raw_bug polling, the API handlers or the reviewer. Concretely, while task A is between BEGIN and COMMIT, task B's UPDATE bugs ... status='dismissed' or 'open' executes on the same sqlite handle inside A's transaction. If A's later tx.execute returns Err, the ? drops tx and rolls back, and B's write vanishes with no error. B's task logs success, and the bug stays in 'processing' with no worker left to retry it. Limits on severity: the window is a few statements wide, so the race is occasional, and a failed transaction is the rarer trigger. The transaction semantics are documented by the code, but I did not read libsql's internals; I assumed Connection::transaction issues BEGIN on the shared handle, which is the standard behaviour. Reading libsql's transaction implementation would confirm that.

locations.why_this_location_matters: Opens a transaction on the single shared connection, so concurrent statements from other tasks are not excluded.
Shows Database wraps exactly one libsql Connection with no pool or serialization.
Adds unbounded concurrent tasks that write through the same Arc<Database> while a dedup transaction may be open.

findings.problem: unlabelled patch-derived text drives unverified bug dismissal
findings.explanation: Consequence: a candidate bug can be permanently set to status 'dismissed' on a single model reply, and nothing independently checks the stored refutation. Reachability: BugInput.problem and reasoning reach VerifySession::initial_user_prompt through process_issue and bug_worker (BugWorker::run rebuilds BugInput from the bugs row). In this commit, process_issue is called only from tests. The design doc says reviewer.rs will queue findings from patch review, and those findings are model output that can quote patch or commit text, which anonymous mailing-list authors control. That producer is not in this diff, so this is an assumption: if the reviewer copies patch-author text into problem or reasoning, attacker-chosen text lands in the Stage 1 prompt. The prompt interpolates 'Problem: {problem}\nReasoning: {reasoning}' with no quoted-content delimiters, and the system prompt never says these fields are data. The prompt does require concrete code proof, and the toolbox lets the model check mainline, which limits the risk. However, process_issue_worker takes verification.is_false_positive on trust. It does no corroboration, such as checking that refutation_evidence cites a file, symbol or line that exists at master_sha. It then calls update_bug_outcome with status 'dismissed', writes the model's refutation_evidence into severity_explanation as the system's own record, and returns Discarded. Nothing re-queues a dismissed row, because lock_raw_bug only selects status = 'raw'. Net effect: a real bug can be silently dropped, and the model's unverified claim is stored as fact. This is Medium rather than higher because it rests on an unverified assumption about the producer, and it needs the model to be steered despite the proof requirement. Confirming evidence would be reviewer.rs passing patch text verbatim into BugInput. Suggested fix: wrap problem and reasoning as quoted data and say so in the system prompt, and require refutation_evidence to cite a checkable location (or send high-severity dismissals to review) before setting 'dismissed'.
